name: Discord Tickets (revamped)
author: egelhaus@ennogelhaus.de
description:
A fork of Discord Tickets, the open-source ticket management bot for Discord, with more features and fewer bugs.

Requires MySQL or PostgreSQL (SQLite is not supported) and a reachable Temporal cluster — all scheduled and durable work (stale tickets, auto-close, exports, cron automations) runs on it, and the bot will not start without one. See docs/installation.md in the repository.

Needs a glibc Node image (the Debian yolks below). Temporal's native addon has no musl build, so Alpine images will not work. Allow ~500 MB of disk.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Installs (or upgrades) Discord Tickets (revamped) into /mnt/server.
#
# Only code paths are replaced: .env, user/ and logs/ are the server's state
# and are left alone, so "Reinstall Server" is also the upgrade procedure.
set -e

BOT_VERSION="${BOT_VERSION:-latest}"
BASE="https://github.com/Gelhaus-Solutions/discordtickets-revamped/releases"
if [ "$BOT_VERSION" = "latest" ]; then
    URL="${BASE}/latest/download/discordtickets-revamped.tar.gz"
else
    URL="${BASE}/download/${BOT_VERSION}/discordtickets-revamped.tar.gz"
fi

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

echo "Downloading ${URL}"
curl -fsSL -o /tmp/bot.tar.gz "$URL"

echo "Replacing the application"
rm -rf src scripts db dist docs node_modules package.json package-lock.json .npmrc .nvmrc .env.example
tar -xzf /tmp/bot.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C /mnt/server
rm -f /tmp/bot.tar.gz

# CI=true keeps preinstall from generating a key here (it is generated below,
# once, so a reinstall never rotates it). DB_PROVIDER= makes postinstall exit
# before touching a database that may not exist yet — @prisma/client's own
# postinstall still runs, so the query engines land in node_modules.
echo "Installing dependencies"
CI=true DB_PROVIDER= npm ci --omit=dev --omit=optional --no-audit --no-fund

if [ ! -f /mnt/server/.env ]; then
    echo "Generating an encryption key"
    KEY=$(head -c 24 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
    {
        echo "# Generated at install time. Everything else lives on the Startup tab."
        echo "# NEVER change ENCRYPTION_KEY once the bot has stored data: ticket"
        echo "# topics, close reasons, feedback and archived messages are encrypted"
        echo "# with it and cannot be read back without the original value."
        echo "ENCRYPTION_KEY=${KEY}"
    } > /mnt/server/.env
    chmod 600 /mnt/server/.env
fi

mkdir -p /mnt/server/user /mnt/server/logs

echo ""
echo "Installed. Before starting, set on the Startup tab:"
echo "  DISCORD_TOKEN, DISCORD_SECRET"
echo "  DB_PROVIDER (mysql or postgresql) and DB_CONNECTION_URL"
echo "  TEMPORAL_ADDRESS (and the TEMPORAL_TLS_* variables if it is not local)"
echo ""

variables.name: Version
variables.description: Release tag to install, or `latest`. Change it and reinstall to upgrade.

variables.name: Discord bot token
variables.description: From the Bot page of your application in the Discord developer portal.

variables.name: Discord client secret
variables.description: From the OAuth2 page of your application in the Discord developer portal.

variables.name: Database provider
variables.description: `mysql` or `postgresql`. SQLite is not supported by this fork.

variables.name: Database URL
variables.description: e.g. postgresql://user:password@host:5432/tickets or mysql://user:password@host:3306/tickets

variables.name: Encryption key
variables.description: Leave EMPTY to use the key generated during installation (recommended). NEVER change this once the bot has data — every encrypted field becomes unreadable.

variables.name: JWT secret
variables.description: Optional. Signs dashboard sessions; derived from the encryption key when empty. Set it to your old ENCRYPTION_KEY if you are migrating from upstream and want existing sessions to survive.

variables.name: External URL
variables.description: The URL users reach the dashboard on, with no trailing slash. Must match the OAuth redirect URI in the Discord developer portal. Leave empty to use http://<server ip>:<port>.

variables.name: Internal URL
variables.description: Optional. An address the bot can reach itself on, bypassing your reverse proxy.

variables.name: Trust proxy
variables.description: Set to true only when running behind a reverse proxy you control.

variables.name: Temporal address
variables.description: Host or IP of the Temporal frontend. Required — the bot will not start without it.

variables.name: Temporal port
variables.description: Temporal frontend port, usually 7233.

variables.name: Temporal namespace
variables.description: Temporal namespace. For Temporal Cloud this is `<namespace>.<account>`.

variables.name: Temporal task queue
variables.description: Leave as-is unless you run several bots against one namespace.

variables.name: Temporal deployment name
variables.description: Worker Deployment name used for versioning.

variables.name: Temporal TLS
variables.description: true for Temporal Cloud or any cluster reached over a network you do not control. Plaintext gRPC on 7233 has no authentication at all, and workflow state includes ticket data.

variables.name: Temporal client certificate
variables.description: Path to the mTLS client certificate, e.g. /home/container/certs/client.pem (upload it with the file manager).

variables.name: Temporal client key
variables.description: Path to the mTLS client private key, e.g. /home/container/certs/client.key

variables.name: Temporal CA certificate
variables.description: Path to the server root CA, if it is not publicly trusted.

variables.name: Temporal server name
variables.description: SNI override, if your cluster needs one.

variables.name: Superusers
variables.description: Comma-separated Discord user IDs with operator rights: settings for every guild, any transcript, and service API keys. Set it to your own ID, or leave it empty.

variables.name: Public bot
variables.description: Set to true only if anyone may invite this bot. Disables stale-ticket handling.

variables.name: Publish commands
variables.description: Register slash commands on every start.

variables.name: Invalidate tokens
variables.description: Set to an ISO date to invalidate every session and API key issued before it.

variables.name: Override archive
variables.description: Set to false to disable message archiving for every server.

variables.name: Disable encryption
variables.description: Leave false. Encryption protects ticket content at rest.

variables.name: CPU limit
variables.description: Optional cap on the worker thread pool. Defaults to the number of available cores.

variables.name: Stats URL
variables.description: Optional Houston-compatible endpoint for anonymous usage stats. Nothing is reported when empty.

variables.name: Sentry DSN
variables.description: Optional error reporting.

variables.name: Data directory
variables.description: Where .env, user/ and logs/ live. Do not change.

variables.name: Application directory
variables.description: Where the code lives. Do not change.

variables.name: Node environment
variables.description: Do not change.

variables.name: Sentry environment
variables.description: Optional. Labels events in Sentry (e.g. production, staging). Defaults to the app's NODE_ENV.

variables.name: Sentry trace sample rate
variables.description: Optional. Fraction of requests and interactions traced, 0-1. Empty means 0.1.

variables.name: Sentry profiling rate
variables.description: Optional. Fraction of traced transactions profiled, 0-1. Empty means 1.0.

variables.name: Sentry logs
variables.description: Optional. Forward the bot's log output to Sentry Logs. true or false.

variables.name: Sentry log level
variables.description: Optional. Minimum level forwarded when Sentry logs are on. 'debug' includes every database query.

variables.name: Sentry metrics
variables.description: Optional. Application metrics such as tickets opened/closed and latencies. true or false.

variables.name: Sentry send PII
variables.description: Optional. Sends Discord user IDs and IP addresses. These belong to your members, not to you - leave false unless you need them.

variables.name: Dashboard Sentry DSN
variables.description: Optional. Browser error reporting for the web dashboard. This DSN is served to every visitor, so use a separate project from the bot's.

variables.name: Dashboard trace rate
variables.description: Optional. Browser performance tracing, 0-1. Empty means off.

variables.name: Dashboard replay rate
variables.description: Optional. Session Replay sampling, 0-1. Recordings mask all text and block all media, but still capture staff activity on pages showing ticket transcripts. Empty means off.

variables.name: Dashboard replay-on-error rate
variables.description: Optional. Session Replay sampling for sessions that hit an error, 0-1. Empty means off.

variables.name: Transcript storage driver
variables.description: Where ticket transcripts are kept. "local" writes them under the data directory and is right for almost every install. "s3" uses S3-compatible object storage and needs the bucket settings below.

variables.name: S3 bucket
variables.description: Bucket transcripts are written to. Required when the storage driver is "s3".

variables.name: S3 endpoint
variables.description: Leave EMPTY for real AWS. For MinIO and other self-hosted gateways, the base URL, e.g. http://minio:9000

variables.name: S3 region
variables.description: Region the bucket lives in. Self-hosted gateways usually ignore this but still expect a value.

variables.name: S3 key prefix
variables.description: Optional prefix within the bucket, e.g. "production/". Leave empty to write to the bucket root.

variables.name: S3 path-style addressing
variables.description: Required by MinIO and most self-hosted gateways. Leave true unless your provider says otherwise.

variables.name: S3 access key ID
variables.description: Leave EMPTY to use the AWS SDK credential chain (instance roles). Otherwise the access key for the bucket.

variables.name: S3 secret access key
variables.description: Secret for the access key above. Leave EMPTY when using the credential chain.

variables.name: S3 session token
variables.description: Only needed for temporary credentials. Leave EMPTY otherwise.
